title: How do noise-cancelling headphones erase sound?

scenes.text: How do noise-cancelling headphones erase sound?
Sound is just air pressure moving in waves, with highs and lows.
Tiny microphones on the outside of each earcup listen to the noise around you.
A chip flips that wave upside down, and the speaker plays the exact opposite.
When a high meets a low, they cancel out, so the noise fades before it reaches your ear.
It works best on steady sounds, like a plane engine. Follow for more.
